title: platform-telemetry-cost-playbook-for-product-engineering-2026
author: Priya Nanduri
content:
Title: Platform telemetry & cost playbook for product engineering

Summary
This playbook is for product engineering teams building user-facing features on top of Redwood’s inference platform. It defines a shared vocabulary, dashboard and alert patterns, cost-attribution signals, and a step-by-step investigation and action workflow that balances product quality, latency SLOs, and operational cost. The goal is to give product teams a practical, repeatable route to evaluate cost impact, iterate safely, and engage platform/ops when needed.

Who should use this doc
- Product engineers and PMs shipping LLM-backed features
- Engineering managers reviewing rollout economics
- Platform operators who will be contacted for escalations

When to use it
- Pre-launch: establish telemetry baselines and cost budgets
- During rollout: monitor early token/latency anomalies and cost spikes
- Post-rollout: reconcile actual spend, tagging, and retention windows

Key principles
- Measure close to the cost surface: attribute at the token, route, and model-variant level where possible.
- Prioritize product-level KPIs first (perceived latency, error rate), then cost as a secondary constraint with explicit budgets.
- Safety-first alerts: alert on potential customer impact, not raw dollar movement. Use cost alerts for ops and cadence reviews.
- Make tradeoffs auditable: keep canonical query definitions and dashboards in the platform repo.

Required ownership and contacts
- Product engineering: owns feature instrumentation, route labels, and baseline queries.
- Platform Observability: maintains the canonical cost dashboards and sampling manifests.
- Finance/Cost Ops: provides monthly reconciliation and tagging rules.
- Oncall: SRE/Platform oncall is the escalation target for automated cost controls.

Definitions and canonical signals
- token_count: total generated tokens per request (server-side counter).
- token_cost_estimate: derived metric = token_count * model_unit_cost + runtime_overhead.
- route_id: logical API route or product feature label.
- model_variant: the exact model/version / quantization profile used for inference.
- latency_p50/p95/p99: standard latency quantiles measured at front-door and runtime.
- error_rate: HTTP 5xx + model mis-invocation rate.

Dashboards to create (minimum viable set)
1) Product cost rollup (per-week, per-route)
   - Key panels: total token_count, token_cost_estimate, top-10 routes by spend, spend trend vs. budget.
   - Filters: route_id, team, region, model_variant.
2) Quality vs cost scatter (per-route)
   - X axis: token_cost_estimate per request, Y axis: perceived latency (front-door p95), point size = request volume.
   - Purpose: find high-cost low-value outliers.
3) Real-time token surge watch
   - Stream panel: 1m token_count, 5m rolling token_cost_estimate, anomaly band (expected ±2σ).
4) Model-variant economics matrix
   - Table: model_variant | avg token_count | avg token_cost_estimate | p95 latency | error_rate | last_deployed_by

Dashboard implementation notes
- All dashboard panels must reference canonical PromQL/SQL named queries (store queries in telemetry/query-definitions repo).
- Use consistent timezones (UTC) and sample windows: 1m for real-time, 1h/24h for trends.
- Provide drilldowns to raw traces and a canonical Kibana/Trace link.

Alerting patterns and thresholds
- Product-impact alerts (paged to product + oncall):
  1) p95 front-door latency increases > 40% vs baseline AND error_rate > 0.5% sustained 5m.
  2) Route-level request drop > 20% with no upstream deployment in last 10m.
- Cost-awareness alerts (email/Slack to product + cost-ops):
  1) 24h spend for route > 2x expected daily budget AND token_cost_estimate growth rate > 50% 12h.
  2) Sustained model_variant cost per request > baseline + 30% for 6h.
- Automated mitigation actions (must be gated by an `operator_reauth` flag and runbook):
  - soft-throttle route to 80% traffic to force degrade safely
  - route fallback to cheaper model_variant (see safe-fallback checklist below)

Investigation and response workflow (step-by-step)
1) Triage (product engineer) — 0-15m
   - Validate alert: check dashboard, compare against baseline windows (previous 7 days).
   - Correlate with deploys: query CI/CD tag and model release events.
   - Run a quick per-user sampling query to determine per-customer impact.
2) Contain (product engineer + platform oncall) — 15-45m
   - If cost spike is due to runaway requests: apply a rate limit or quota at the ingress.
   - If due to model degradation producing longer token outputs: apply a soft-model swap to the cheaper variant (see safe-fallback checklist).
   - Document commands and actions in the incident channel.
3) Stabilize (platform) — 45m-3h
   - Execute a controlled canary swap on a small shard of traffic. Monitor quality regressions using predefined eval prompt set.
   - If stable, scale the fallback; if not, revert and open an investigation.
4) Reconcile (product + finance) — 1-7 days
   - Run full cost attribution, update budget estimates, and identify long-term mitigations (prompt engineering, batching, cache).

Safe-fallback checklist (must be completed before automated fallback)
- Confirm model_variant compatibility: identical tokenizer and prompt contract.
- Verify evaluation set: run 50 synthetic prompts and validate BLEU/ROUGE or product MP metrics.
- Confirm no new PII/data-routing constraints for fallback variant.
- Notify stakeholders (product, security, customer-success) via preconfigured channel.
- Record fallback as a short-lived feature flag with owner and rollback window.

Sample runbook commands (examples only)
- Inspect top spenders: 
  SQL: SELECT route_id, SUM(token_count) as tokens, SUM(token_cost_estimate) as cost FROM telemetry.requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '24 hours' GROUP BY route_id ORDER BY cost DESC LIMIT 25;
- Trigger soft throttle (CLI):
  ./platform-ctl routes throttle --route=my-feature --limit=80% --reason="cost-spike-2026-02-03" --owner=product-oncall
- Canary swap (CLI):
  ./platform-ctl rollout model-swap --route=my-feature --from=redwood/gptx-quant-8bit --to=redwood/gptx-fp16 --canary=5% --monitor=/dashboards/model-variant-eval

Telemetry and tagging checklist (pre-launch)
| Field | Required | Purpose | Owner |
|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| route_id | yes | logical product surface | product eng |
| team | yes | cost rollups | product eng |
| customer_id | recommended | top-customer attribution | product eng |
| model_variant | yes | accurate unit economics | infra/platform |
| experiment_id | recommended | A/B cost impact | product eng |
| retention_tier | yes | trace/log retention policy | platform |

Common root causes and mitigations
- Root cause: prompt changes causing longer generations
  - Mitigations: add max_tokens cap, introduce model-side length heuristics, evaluate prompt templating.
- Root cause: traffic shift from a partner causing burst of requests
  - Mitigations: add per-tenant soft quotas, burst credits, and route-level throttles.
- Root cause: abrupt model-version change with higher token churn
  - Mitigations: require pre-deploy economic smoke tests and a canary stage with cost hooks.

SLOs and budgets (recommended defaults)
- Product-level latency: p95 front-door <= 600ms for interactive features; stricter targets for sync UIs.
- Incident escalation budget: product owners must be notified for any >25% daily budget overshoot.
- Monthly experiment cost budget: any A/B experiment must have an upfront cost cap and an automatic kill threshold.

Playbook for product onboarding (2-week checklist)
Week 0 (planning):
1) Define expected routes and assign route_id.
2) Draft provisional cost budget and add to project PR.
Week 1 (integration):
1) Instrument route_id and model_variant tagging in requests.
2) Add sample queries for dashboard panels to telemetry/query-definitions.
3) Run a 24h smoke test with synthetic traffic to record baselines.
Week 2 (go-live and guardrails):
1) Configure alerts for product-impact and cost-awareness thresholds.
2) Add runbook stub and assign a named oncall owner for first 72h post-launch.
3) Schedule a postmortem + budget reconciliation meeting at day 7.

Appendix: example Slack escalation template
Channel: #prod-my-feature-ops
Message template:
"ALERT: Route my-feature exceeding 2x daily budget. p95 latency = $LATENCY, token_rate = $TOKEN_RATE, top-customer = $TOP_CUSTOMER. Actions taken: soft-throttle applied (80%), canary fallback initiated. Paging: @platform-oncall @product-owner. Runbook: <link>."
